stories.summary:
https://buffalonews.com/sports/professional/nfl/bills/article_504aae18-8d82-4a36-b341-729384a9599e.html?gift=1&gift_token=01681adf-2712-48aa-b484-d99d9eda3d34



	 



	As usual, a great read from Jim Kubiak.  Top line review:



	 



	"It appears, in this Brady era, that he is giving more of a load on Allen...The turnovers, combined with his late game decisions, tell us that a change in coaching strategy [is needed]... with an emphasis on proven QB management principles..."



	 



	Highlights:



	-Brady taking the ball after winning the toss ala Detroit (note: Chargers won the toss and elected to kick so Brady did not make the choice there) defies conventional wisdom.  My take-- Brady has moved passed being aggressive to being aggressively stupid.



	 



	-Patriots were doing nothing exotic on defense, not a lot of exotic looks or blitzes



	 



	- Bills from the jump got away from running the ball.  Pass happy.  Last year they passed 45% of time, this year 50%.  Even more so v. Pats



	 



	-Too much Allen leads to more bad Josh plays, including muffed handoff to Cook, behind-the -back pass (pure panic and lucky to get away with it), a wide-open miss to Shakir on 3rd and 4, blown read on two-point conversion and interception to end the game.



	 



	Other stuff:



	-Checkdown screen pass to the WR that everyone hates was actually a good call under the circumstances and would have worked but Palmer blew the block.



	 



	Two-point conversion play gave Allen three options. Corner pass to Coleman, pass to Palmer, and built-in TE delay. Without pressure, Allen never looked for that built-in option.



	Interception at end-- Allen completely loses situational awareness.  Loses focus on ball security and clock management.



	 



	Bottom line for me, Brady needs to be less of Allen's pal and more parental.  He should not coddle Allen as it brings out the bad parts of Allen's game.  Kubiak concludes that if Brady does not get this team more focused on ball security and taking what is there instead of being overly aggressive, this team will not get to where it wants to go.

stories.title: Sabres Tame Wild In Third Period Comeback
stories.summary:
Buffalo refuse to be beaten, defeat Wild in overtime



Boxscore



Score: Buffalo Sabres 3-2 Minnesota Wild (OT)Shots: BUF 28-20 MIN



Buffalo Sabres Goals: Östlund 1 (Power, Dahlin); Thompson 2 (Krebs); Power 1 (Kulich)Minnesota Wild Goals: Yurov 1 PPG (Spurgeon, Coleman); Shabanov 1 (Hughes, McCarron)



Quick Thoughts



Low Event First



Colten Ellis made his first start of the season between the pipes and the Sabres played a quiet, low-event first period which was perfect to get him settled in. He looked calm and collected in goal, and made a big save late in the period stonewalling Kirill Kaprizov in the blue paint to keep the scores level. 



An early power play was not as abysmal as the other man advantage attempts have been, but of course, Buffalo couldn’t score. 



After getting demoted late in the last game, Ryan McLeod started the game very well making his presence felt whenever he was on the ice. Louis Crevier hasn’t had an ideal Buffalo debut either, but he looked good in the first period here throwing himself around before jamming up the puck on the penalty kill to burn nearly half a minute of clock. 




Louis Crevier essentially killed the last 22 seconds of a PK by himself, in his own zone. #LetsGoBuffalo #MnWild pic.twitter.com/S61DJT5noK— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 6, 2026




The Sabres penalty kill came into the game having given up two goals in five attempts, but ended the period creating more chances on the Wild’s two power plays than the visitors did. The period ended with the Wild leading in shots 4-3, and leading in scoring chances 8-2 as well. 



Where’s The Consistency?



The second period started with more of the same as the first. It was mostly uneventful hockey with Buffalo guilty more than once of looking to play the perfect pass, waiting to take the perfect shot, and you can’t do that against a Wild team that plays hard and fast. 



Josh Norris and Tage Thompson on the top line looked anonymous for long periods. However after another successful penalty kill, things started to heat up at KeyBank Center.



With seven to play in the second period, the Sabres were in the attacking zone when Peyton Krebs ran into a Wild defenseman in an attempt to get back onside. To the arena’s displeasure that got called for interference and the visitors had the man advantage for the fourth time. They finally mustered a shot on goal, their first in four power plays and Danila Yurov’s shot went off Mattias Samuelsson’s stick and snuck in between Ellis’ shoulder and the near post. Unfortunate. 



What happened next was anything but unfortunate however. Less than two minutes later, Norris got blocked off by Michael McCarron in almost identical fashion as what had happened with Krebs. This time though, no penalty was called and even as the home crowd howled with derision, Quinn Hughes charged down the ice, fanned on a shot from the slot but Maxim Shabanov following up behind him made no mistake with a low shot through the five-hole to beat Ellis again. Even as chants of “refs suck refs suck” rained down from the arena, the score was 2-0.




The same interference play that results in a penalty against the Sabres and subsequent power play goal, now doesn't get called, and the Wild immediately score2-0 Minnesota pic.twitter.com/wxB0U3DVRK— Crossing Swords ⚔️ (@CrossSwordsPod) October 7, 2026




Ruff looked like he lost his patience with his top line towards the end of the period, swapping Krebs and Norris – remember this for later. Better period from the Sabres despite giving up two goals, winning the scoring chances 8-5.



Fortune Favors The (Buffalo) Brave



The Sabres needed to come out in the third period with a jump in their step, and they did just that. As they buzzed around the Wild net they were leaving more spaces behind them, but with three minutes or so in Buffalo did well cycling the puck in the Minnesota zone and had the visitors chasing ghosts as Rasmus Dahlin and Owen Power took perimeter shots before Noah Östlund went to the goal and was rewarded. Power’s shot deflected off a Wild player in front of the goal before going in off the Sabres’ forward’s shin to make it 2-1, game back on.  




The Sabres get rewarded after good puck movement around the Minnesota zone.  Power's pass goes off Noah Ostlund's shinpad an in, 2-1 #LetsGoBuffalo #MnWild pic.twitter.com/1IapFfmlGr— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 7, 2026




With the crowd given life, they started making their presence felt, but not before the Wild rang another shot off the ironworks, this time from Hughes. Halfway through the third, the Sabres lost the puck in the defensive zone but the game leveler then came from a heads-up moment from Krebs. He corraled the puck from a broken play and fed it to Thompson in the slot and his one-timer beat Jesper Wallstedt on the blocker side and just like that it was 2-2. 




Peyton Krebs finds Tage Thompson, 2-2 #LetsGoBuffalo #MnWild pic.twitter.com/Pr6cc9igQ3— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 7, 2026




Benson’s reputation as ‘The Rat’ has gone around the league already – late in the third Jack Quinn had two good shooting chances stopped by Wallstedt, but as Benson rushed the net defenseman Jonas Brodin went crashing into his goalie and immediately a couple of Wild jumped the grinning Benny. 



An ill-advised high stick from Olli Maatta on Norris with less than four minutes to play sent the Sabres to the power play, still looking for their first goal on the man-advantage this season. The puck deflected off Spurgeon and fell to Thompson in the slot and he pushed it goalwards but Wallstedt made a brilliant glove save to keep things level. The Sabres kept the puck in the zone and moved the Wild around before Dahlin’s shot from the blue line was also gloved by the goalie. 



Buffalo had another couple of late attempts but again Wallstedt stood firm as the game headed to overtime, with the Sabres leading 23-18 overall in shots and 12-3 in scoring chances in the third. 



He’s Got The Power



Into overtime we went, and with the Wild trying to pair Boldy with Hughes, Ellis made a huge save on the former. Off that rush the Sabres had a 2-on-1 and Wallstedt foiled Kulich with the blocker. 



Thompson then dangled through the defense but couldn’t get a shot off, before cycling back around and firing off a shot that blasted Wallstedt’s stick out of his grasp. 



Quinn then made a huge defensive play to stop Boldy as he attacked, but couldn’t get the return pass to try and score on the rush back. Tage had another chance as we went into a minute left in the game, the puck felt to Kulich behind the goal and he looked to find Sabres’ player of the game Power steaming down the slot and he slammed his shot into the goal with 37 seconds left for the winner. 




Owen Power wins the game in overtime, 3-2.#LetsGoBuffalo #MnWild pic.twitter.com/foon7IGMMJ— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 7, 2026




At The Horn



Owen Power had 28:21 of ice time tonight going +2 and was very good for most of that. Paired up with Rasmus Dahlin, the Sabres were dominant at times, leading to the third period where they pretty much controlled the narrative to come back into the game. He finished last season strong, and has picked up where he left off this season too. He was nearly off-the-charts good!




NHL Game Score Impact Card for Buffalo Sabres on 2026-10-06: pic.twitter.com/sNyjVqavqQ— HockeyStatCards (@hockeystatcards) October 7, 2026




Power also did this tonight. 




Owen Power made Trenin look silly #LetsGoBuffalo #MnWild pic.twitter.com/JSdyuGuHHt— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 7, 2026




Colten Ellis played well tonight, and has allayed any fears that last season was a flash in the pan. Granted it’s just one game, but it’s a good sign. 



Two games into a five-game homestand, and two wins on the board. Let’s keep that going.

stories.title: The reverse trap game
stories.summary:
I forget who it was, but probably my favorite comment from the original thread was talking about how if players don't have situations where they're at risk to be less motivated than they also don't have situations where they will likely be more motivated. These are highly competitive athletes and they're spending all week listening about how they suck. Josh Allen sucks, Joe Brady sucks, the defense sucks, everybody sucks. This is a proud team, any human being with a pulse of competitive spirit is going to approach the next situation galvanized and with a lot energy. It is a situation where good teams typically respond and historically that is exactly what we have done. We are 4-2 since 2025 as a straight up underdog.  



	 



	



	 



	Remember we had no chance at beating Baltimore, twice. Kansas City multiple times. The Lions a few years back on the road. The Rams in the opener in this same building. This team responds in these exact situations. If you don't think that is the case, put on your objective glasses with this Rams team. Blown out by the 49ers, a win vs a back up QB, the Denver game which was a toss up, and last second win at Philadelphia without Barkley, without DaVonte Smith. The Rams, like us, want to run a lot of 12 and 13 personnel. The top two TE's are not healthy. They rank 15th in EPA offense.  This is a team playing more off reputation at the moment than actual results and maybe some of the same can be said about us, but they rank 7th in DVOA to our 4th. So it's not even as if the advanced data is aligning with the general vibe on TBD. 



	 



	This is all to say, it is not like we are facing some insurmountable match up here. It's an elite spot for us to bring our A game, and I think we get it done.

stories.summary:
Buffalo continues early season homestand against Minnesota



Buffalo Sabres (1-1-0) vs. Minnesota Wild (2-0-0)



Puck Drop: 7 p.m. ET | KeyBank Center, Buffalo, N.Y.



TV: MSG-B, MINNHL, DAZN, ESPN+, Fubo



Radio: WGR 550, Sirius XM (app)



Know Your Opponent

PP: 5th, 42.9% (3-for-7) [Sabres: 26th, 0.0% (0-for-8)]



PK: 5th, 100.0% (7-for-7) [Sabres: 29th, 60.0% (3-for-5)]



Season Series: Sabres 1-0-1 vs. Wild in 2025-26 season



What to Watch



1. Sabres turn to Ellis in net



After a pair of subpar performances from Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen to begin the season, Buffalo will look to second-year goalie Colten Ellis to start in net Tuesday against Minnesota.



Ellis, who turned 26 on Monday, had fine numbers during his first NHL season, playing in 16 games for the Sabres and finishing with a .903 save percentage to go with 0.32 goals saved above expected, according to Hockeystats.com. He followed that up this preseason with some strong showings as well, stopping 35-of-38 shots in three games played.



Keeping three goalies on the roster allows the Sabres to rotate netminders more than most teams, and the coaching staff seemed content to ride the hot hand during much of last season. With Luukkonen’s shaky start and Alex Lyon’s injury, a strong performance from Ellis against Minnesota may just earn him the starter’s net again on Thursday, and potentially, going forward.



2. A power play fix?



Stop me if you’ve heard this one before: the Sabres are making a tweak to try and spark their dormant power play.



With Buffalo starting the year 0-for-8 on the man advantage, Noah Ostlund has been promoted to the top unit in place of Josh Doan, who dropped to the second unit. Ostlund provides some extra playmaking ability to the first unit, but it remains to be seen just how many chances he’ll have with the puck to use that ability. After Monday’s practice, Sabres coach Lindy Ruff specifically mentioned Ostlund shooting left-handed as a reason for the change, as it helps the unit line up more evenly.



“As soon as you start scoring, everybody will calm down,” Ruff said of the power play struggles. “You know that every power play is going to make some mistakes, but I want them to believe in the process that we’re going through, and continue to stay with it.”



3. Always a Wild one



You can always seem to count on Buffalo and Minnesota to produce some excitement when they meet.



Nine of the last 10 matchups between the Sabres and Wild have been decided by one goal, with six of those games going to overtime. A significant factor in nearly all those meetings has been Minnesota’s star forward Kirill Kaprizov, who has tallied a point in all nine of his career games against the Sabres, totaling seven goals and seven assists. 



With Kaprizov, who’s off to a strong start with three goals so far this season, and plenty more scoring threats suiting up for both teams, another overtime thriller could be in store.



Injury Notes



The Wild continue to be without top pair defenseman Brock Faber, who suffered a skull fracture during the preseason, and they may be down a top center for Tuesday’s game as well, with Danila Yurov (upper-body) a game-time decision.



As for the Sabres, forward Jason Zucker (sports hernia) and goalie Alex Lyon (upper-body) both returned to the ice for optional morning skate on Tuesday, though Ruff indicated Zucker is still a couple weeks away returning, and Lyon does not have a timetable. Both of them, alongside defenseman Conor Timmins (lower-body), remain on injured reserve.

Sabres rally for late win against shorthanded Blackhawks
stories.summary:
Score: Buffalo Sabres 4, Chicago Blackhawks 3



Shots: Buffalo 28, Chicago 15



Buffalo Sabres Goals: Quinn (Metsa); Thompson (Crevier, Norris); Dahlin (Krebs, Samuelsson); Kulich (Power, Thompson)



Chicago Blackhawks Goals: Donato (Vlasic, Lardis); Bertuzzi (Teravainen, Vlasic); Moore (Frondell, Vlasic)



The Buffalo Sabres sneak past the Chicago Blackhawks, who were down number one defenseman Bowen Byram and top player Connor Bedard, 4-3 in their first win of the season.



First Period River Hockey



Though they were pressured on the first shift, thanks in part to an amped-up Jordan Greenway, the Sabres dictated the pace for the first five minutes of the first. They had their legs ready early, and while they couldn’t cash in for an early lead, it led to a handful of scoring chances. 



That early work would be for naught, though, as Ryan Donato would bury a chance past Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen at the 8:00 minute mark of the period to give the Blackhawks an early lead. Blackhawks defenseman Alex Vlasic carried the puck low, and while four Sabres were in the area of the crease, Vlasic was able to find the open space to set up for Donato, who made no mistake. 



This goal did not discourage the Sabres, rather it seemed to invigorate them. The Benson-Ostlund-Quinn trio combined for a couple of high-quality chances, while the line of Ryan McLeod, Konsta Helenius, and Peyton Krebs generated a quick strike chance. This, once again, was all for naught. 



At the 11:49 mark, just after their scoring chance they couldn’t capitalize on, that line, particularly Helenius and Krebs, helped contribute to yet another defensive blunder, as Tyler Bertuzzi was left all alone in the crease, able to bury the easiest tap-in a player can have, thanks to a feed from Teuvo Teravaianen. 



Despite the 2-0 hole they dug themselves, the Sabres kept pushing but couldn’t beat Blackhawks goalie Spencer Knight. Sabres captain Rasmus Dahlin was robbed once on a cross-ice feed from Quinn, then again on a chance in the high-slot a few seconds later, when the Blackhawks also benefited from an early whistle, as officials ruled Knight had the puck covered when he almost certainly did not. 



Finally, though, persistence paid off, as Quinn got the Sabres on the board on their 13th shot of the period. Quinn found space, carried the puck to the high slot, and using Blackhawks defenseman Kevin Korchinski as a screen, sniped the corner to cut the deficit to 2-1. While Zach Metsa got the lone assist, the goal wouldn’t have happened without a nice pinch by Louis Crevier, who used his reach to keep the play alive. 



While the score went into the first intermission at 2-1, the crowd did get one last thing to cheer about before the horn sounded, as Patrick Kane, who was met with a cacophony of boos the whole game, got lit up by Mattias Samuelsson in the dying seconds of the third. 



Knight was the story of the first for the Blackhawks, who had two xGoals of chances put on him and was able to allow only one. It was overall a very “River Hockey” type period with high paced play and defensive lapses. 



A full 60 (pages)



The Sabres came out firing in the second, generating a few shots in the first few minutes, and missing on a few others, with McLeod unable to center a pass to the slot and Quinn overskating a puck. Knight also made a nice glove save on Sam Carrick from the slot, then another on Quinn a couple minutes later. 



The Sabres kept the pressure on and were rewarded with the equalizer just six minutes into the second. Thompson won a faceoff back to Crevier, who ripped a shot from the point that deflected off Thompson’s stick for his first of the season. 



The Sabres were not satisfied with a tie, as the pressure continued relentlessly after the game was tied up. Knight had to keep his head in the game, quite literally, as he used his mask to deny Olen Zellweger of a potential go ahead goal. 



The game hit a lull in the middle part of the second, as both teams defaulted to feeling each other out. The Blackhawks would get the game’s first power play almost 12 minutes into the frame, as Josh Doan committed a hooking penalty. The Sabres had a huge question mark over the head of their penalty kill after their first game, but they answered the bell on their first opportunity of the game, though Luukkonen did have to make a really nice save in tight as the Blackhawks power play expired. 



A flurry of chances, highlighted by Helenius being denied on a shot in tight off a behind the net feed by McLeod, still couldn’t give the Sabres the lead, though the constant pressure did give them their first power play of the game. 



As has been the case for the past two seasons, the power play killed the momentum for the Sabres, as Thompson single handedly killed zone pressure on three separate occasions, one of which led to a breakaway that Luukkonen had to stop. The second unit got a nice look, but as the power play expired, the Blackhawks found themselves on a two-on-one rush with McLeod as the only Sabre back. Oliver Moore, who came out of the penalty box, made no mistake, as Luukkonen was unable to get enough to keep the puck out of the net, giving the Blackhawks the lead back, 3-2. 



It’s a save the Sabres’ goalie could have made, but it was yet another opportunistic play by the Blackhawks, who preferred quality over quantity in this game, particularly in the period, where they only mustered four shots on goal. 



Lock In and Lock Down



The third period started with an early Sabres power play, as local villain Kane found himself in the box, but as it stands there is no more efficient way to protect a lead than to give the Sabres a power play. 



The Sabres then spent most of the third period attempting to carry the puck into the Blackhawks’ zone, only for them to get met at the blue line and have to chase the puck back. However, the breakthrough finally happened, off the stick of the captain, Rasmus Dahlin, thanks to a nice feed from Peyton Krebs on a counter-rush. Dahlin took the pass in the high slot and sniped it home to tie it up for the Sabres again. 



The Sabres would have another great chance a few minutes later as Quinn found himself all alone in front of the net after Benson broke up a play at center ice to set him up. Quinn however slid the puck wide, unable to give the Sabres their first lead of the game. 



While it looked like the Sabres would get a late chance on the power play, as Cole Smith found himself in the box for tripping, Benson would answer with a tripping penalty of his own to put it at a four on four. Thankfully, this is advantageous for the Sabres.



At the end of a shift, Thompson and Kulich found themselves on a two-on-one, and while Kulich couldn’t bury the shot, he would get another chance. The puck found Owen Power, who found Kulich yet again, who made no mistake on his second opportunity, giving the Sabres the lead, 4-3, with his first of the season, with just 6:40 left on the clock. 



After taking the lead, the team locked in defensively, allowing the Blackhawks just one shot on goal after taking the lead. 



Wrap Up



All in all, it was a bit of a sloppy game from the Sabres, but they were able to rally against an opponent that was missing their best forward and defenseman. But, they don’t ask how, they ask how many, and a number in the left column is exactly what the Sabres needed.



Other notes



There were a few interesting lineup changes near the end of the game. Metsa played just one shift in the third period, and McLeod was flipped to the fourth line with Carrick and Beck Malenstyn. The group of them did not see the ice after taking the lead. Kulich was bumped up to play with Krebs and Helenius, who contributed to what would be the game winning goal. 



On Kulich, he was clearly very emotional in his post game interview. It had to be a nice moment for him, from thinking he may never play hockey again to scoring a game winner. It should be the first of many he scores over the rest of his NHL career. 



Bowen Byram will have to wait for his Buffalo homecoming moment, as he missed the game tending to a family matter.

stories.title: Game #2 Preview & Open Thread: Sabres vs Blackhawks
stories.summary:
Byram Will Not Play in Buffalo Return



Unfortunately, there is only one “revenge game” tonight. Former defenseman Bowen Byram will not play for Chicago tonight. Blackhawks coach Jeff Blashill said Byram is tending to a family matter. That means Sabres fans will have to wait for Byram’s first game back at KeyBank Center since Buffalo traded him to Chicago this summer. Jordan Greenway is still expected to be in Chicago’s lineup and will face the Sabres for the first time since the trade. Byram’s absence forces Chicago to reshuffle its defense. Kevin Korchinski and Ethan Del Mastro will both make their season debuts after sitting out the Blackhawks’ first two games. Byram didn’t have the best first game, but I’m sure it will improve. Byram got everything he wanted when he was traded: to be the #1 D-man and a big contract, so “revenge” is a little harsh.



Zellweger Is In



There is no longer much uncertainty surrounding Olen Zellweger, and the Byram replacement will get his first look in the blue and gold. Zellweger will make his Sabres season debut tonight after recovering from the concussion he suffered during the preseason against Columbus. He practiced alongside Owen Power on Friday and is listed with Power on Buffalo’s second defense pair in the NHL’s latest projected lineup. That gives Buffalo another high-end skating and puck-moving option on the back end and changes the look of the defense from Thursday’s loss in Columbus. The NHL’s current projection has Matt Grzelcyk returning to the lineup alongside Louis Crevier; they played together in Chicago last year on the third pair, with Zach “fighting” Metsa listed as a scratch.

Final Thoughts



The Byram storyline has changed, but plenty remains around Buffalo’s home opener. Jordan Greenway returns to KeyBank Center in a Blackhawks sweater, Patrick Kane is back in Buffalo, and Olen Zellweger will make his Sabres debut. 



Chicago is also changing two-thirds of its bottom four on defense after surrendering 11 goals through its first two games. For Buffalo, the task remains the same: take advantage of a struggling team, clean up special teams, and establish control early rather than letting Chicago hang around. Last season’s Atlantic Division banner goes up in the rafters tonight.



Then Buffalo gets back to work.

Minus 1: Sammy! Then WHAMMY!



Buffalo got a good chance just seconds into the game when Tage Thompson rang one off the iron. Josh Doan followed that up with a nice pass from Josh Norris, taking the puck right to the net, but Jet Greaves of Columbus made a quality save. The Blue Jackets then put on a strong forecheck but couldn’t get the puck to the net for a shot. Carson Soucy was called for cross-checking Sabres forward Jack Quinn, giving Buffalo’s much-maligned power play its first opportunity of the season.



It didn’t last long.



After fumbling the puck at least twice, TNT was called for hooking, negating the rest of the man advantage. That opened the ice for 4-on-4 play and gave Mattias Samuelsson plenty of room to let one rip. Sammy cashed in with a wicked shot that eluded Greaves. Noah Ostlund and Owen Power picked up the assists on Buffalo’s first goal of the new season.



Ten minutes in, the shots were just 3-2 in favor of the Sabres.



Buffalo picked up its fourth and fifth shots while enjoying some quality zone time, but a Columbus breakout would tie the game. Charlie Coyle tried to split the Sabres defense, which closed in on him, but Coyle made a great play to drop the puck back to an open Cole Sillinger. He fired a snapper past a surprised Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen. The Sabres’ forwards were caught too deep and couldn’t get back to cover the man in the slot.



A little later, Buffalo fumbled the puck in front of its own net with some inopportune passing. Samuelsson had to tie up his man to recover, bringing him down and taking a penalty in the process. Columbus cashed in quickly as Matthew Knies snapped a shot on UPL from about 15 feet out that found the twine. The Jackets had now collected four straight shots and two goals. They added another on their next shot. Adam Fantilli’s long-distance blast had eyes, beating Luukkonen again.



The Sabres’ first-period collapse was painful to watch and incredibly discouraging after scoring first on the road. Buffalo’s new and undermanned defense was certainly not in midseason form, and neither was UPL. The Sabres weren’t aggressive enough defensively, repeatedly backing in instead of challenging the Columbus attack. This was a serious shake-your-head period—one Buffalo desperately needed to put behind it. Would they?



Plus 1: Two on the Board but One Against



A quick turnover to start the period allowed Jack Quinn to bring the game back within one. Buffalo held the puck in at the blue line, where Zach Benson came up with it and quickly dished it to Quinn. Benson then drove to the net, taking a Columbus defender with him. Quinn cut wide, setting himself up for the shot before zipping the puck past Jet Greaves. It was a huge goal to start the middle frame and exactly what the Blue and Gold needed.



Buffalo found some new life after the goal, generating more zone time and pressure. The Sabres would draw a penalty on a strong forecheck as Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen headed to the bench. The whistle eventually blew with the puck rolling in front of Buffalo’s empty net. Mathieu Olivier decided he would break the unwritten rules and fired the puck into the yawning cage, and Sabres defenseman Zach Metsa let him know that wasn’t going to fly, giving him a good shove. The hulking Blue Jackets enforcer then decided to go ham, attacking Metsa and firing away with wild punches. Metsa was clearly overmatched and undersized, but to his credit, Zach hung in there. He absorbed Olivier’s relentless barrage and even managed to sneak in a few shots of his own. Metsa did his best to shield himself from the assault, but where were the refs on that one? A much smaller player was essentially in survival mode against a significantly bigger opponent, and the zebras simply stood back and watched. Way to go, NHL.



Buffalo would receive a five-on-three advantage following the incident, but the Sabres couldn’t cash in. A two-man advantage was the perfect opportunity to tie the game, and good teams find a way to capitalize in those situations. Buffalo didn’t, and it would come back to bite them as Columbus reestablished its two-goal lead. Matthew Knies scored again, giving him three points on the night. The former Toronto Maple Leaf seemed possessed, apparently determined to continue finding success against Buffalo even after leaving the Atlantic Division.



The Sabres would get their fourth power play of the night shortly afterward, but once again failed to score. However, Buffalo continued to keep the pressure on and finally found twine moments after the penalty expired. Konsta Helenius scored his first goal of the season after receiving a beautiful cross-ice pass from Ryan McLeod. Owen Power picked up his second assist of the game on the play as well.



The Sabres generated some good zone time for the remainder of the period, but couldn’t find the equalizer. After 40 minutes, Columbus still held a 4-3 lead.







Minus 2: Sammy’s Double Whammy



Buffalo continued to get some zone time early in the period, generating a few chances while pressing the attack. Benson and Ostlund were standouts among the forward ranks. Luukkonen then came up with his best save of the game, getting a piece of the puck while sliding across the crease to deny a Columbus 2-on-1. He had faced just 16 shots to that point, but four of them had already found the back of the net. He remained focused though.



Owen Power then had his stick slashed in half as Sillenger was sent off the ice. Another chance for the dreaded Buffalo power play. Once again, failure, though the Sabres came close with a shot off the post with 3 seconds left. Columbus was all over the puck carrier and was winning most of the face offs. UPL then came up big again, denying Knies of a hat trick on a breakaway. It wasn’t his best outing for sure but he kept his team in it for much of the third period.



Samuelsson then took his second penalty of the evening, this time for tripping. The Sabres nearly killed it off, but Sean Monahan tipped the puck past UPL with just two seconds remaining on the man advantage. Just like that, Columbus had a 5-3 lead. Both of Sammy’s penalties ultimately resulted in Blue Jackets power-play goals.



Buffalo eventually pulled UPL, and, well, we all know how that usually goes. You have a better chance of hitting the Lotto than the Sabres cashing in on a 6-on-5 advantage. After several more puck fumbles, Mathieu Olivier found the empty net to seal a 6-3 Columbus victory. As discussed before the game, the Sabres simply do not match up well against Columbus, for whatever reason. It was a disappointing way to start the new year, with mental mistakes and poor puck control plaguing Buffalo throughout the night. The defense also failed to attack the way it needed to, allowing the Blue Jackets far too much room to operate.



Overall, it was a frustrating game to watch. The Sabres have plenty of work to do and will need to clean up several problem areas before they take the ice again. What a ginormous disappointment. We waited all summer for THAT???



Final Thoughts:



Once again, special teams were a major issue in this game. The power play went 0-for-5, while the penalty kill managed to go just 1-for-3. There’s your game right there. Those are simply dreadful numbers, and the struggles on the faceoff dot only made matters worse. Draws have been an issue with this group for some time, and tonight was no different. Buffalo won just 41 percent of tonight’s faceoffs, including losing many while on the man advantage.



Rasmus Dahlin and Tage Thompson were very quiet in this game, not a good winning recipe.



The Sabres now turn their attention to the Chicago Blackhawks for their home opener on Saturday, October 3rd, at 7 p.m. at KeyBank Center. Former Buffalo defenseman Bo Byram will make his first return to the building.

What to Watch



1. Sky-high Expectations



“With a rebel yell, more, more, more. More, more, more!”



With the playoff drought monkey finally off the Sabres’ backs, you would have thought that the Sabrehood would be somewhat sated. Instead, one would say expectations are absolutely sky-high going into tonight’s game. The fans are ready for a Cup-run and last season’s eventual elimination was just a blip in that timeline. 



The Sabres are going to be hard-pressed to repeat that ridiculous late-season run – they went 29-9-5 from when the calendar turned to 2026, the best record in the league with only Stanley Cup champions Carolina Hurricanes one point behind them and everyone else chasing their dust.   



2. Maintain The Level



Buffalo has gotten to their division-winning berth last season by playing high intensity hockey, and they will have to quickly find those levels this season too. The Sabres didn’t make any marquee additions over the offseason, and lost core players Alex Tuch and Bowen Byram. It looks like Olen Zellweger is being touted as the Byram replacement, but otherwise the expectation is that youngsters on the team are going to all make a respective step up.  



Even more importantly, can the three-headed goalie monster replicate their incredible form from last season? Their .899 combined save percentage was second in the league and carried them to the playoffs.



3. A Pesky Opponent



Columbus have been a bit of a bogey team for the Sabres for some time now, their hard-hitting physical game has frustrated the Sabres often enough over the last few seasons with Buffalo 6-7-2 in the last five years. The Blue Jackets traded away Kirill Marchenko and Elvis Merzlikins and added Matthew Knies, and will have to decide who they really are as they seek a new identity. 



Led by star defenseman Zach Werenski and young center Adam Fantilli and boosted by veterans Charlie Coyle, Sean Monahan and Valeri Nichushkin with another young playmaker in Kent Johnson, there’s still lots of talent in this side. Goalie Jet Greaves will be looking to make an impression too, this is a dangerous opponent.

stories.title: Buffalo Sabres sign defenseman Louis Crevier to four-year extension
stories.summary:
Even before he has played his first game for the Buffalo Sabres tonight, Louis Crevier has decided he wants to stick around, signing a four-year contract extension worth $16 million ($4M AAV). 



The 6’8″ defenseman had signed a two-year, $1.8 million contract with the Chicago Blackhawks on July 17, 2025, before being traded to the Buffalo Sabres in June 2026, and this extension marks a big raise for the hulking player. The Sabres now have five defensemen signed through the end of the 2028-29 season, which is a sign of stability at the position. 




The Buffalo Sabres have signed defenseman Louis Crevier to a four-year extension with an AAV of $4 million. pic.twitter.com/n57zNRKcu3— Buffalo Sabres PR (@SabresPR) October 1, 2026




Crevier joined the Sabres as part of the return for star defenseman Bowen Byram who went to the Windy City. The 25-year-old dman has featured in 134 career NHL games after getting drafted 188th overall by the Blackhawks in the 2020 NHL Draft. He has scored 10 goals with 22 assists, and was ranked second in Chicago last season in a couple of key defensive metrics with 95 blocked shots and 124 hits.



Lindy Ruff is happy with what he has seen so far in practice and in the preseason games – 



“When I’ve watched him at practice, we’ve had lots of discussions about him. We’ve watched him in the games, he’s moved the puck well and skated well. There was a little concern coming off [shoulder] surgery this summer, but everything looks great. I think this will be a great fit for our hockey club.”



Crevier for his part just wanted to settle his future before the season started – 



“I’m really happy. It’s something I’ve worked at for awhile now, and I’m just super glad it’s behind me. Just having stability, I think will help me a ton to play hockey. 



“Everyone was really welcoming, and since it happened in the summer, I was free to process more-and-more information, learn names and stuff, even before I came into Buffalo. I think that helped a lot. It was just super easy, honestly.”



About his fellow blue-liners, the dman was very complimentary – 



“I think they’re all really good players, so it helps a lot. In Chicago, it was the same even earlier in the year last year. We were playing seven defensemen, so I feel like I’m used to playing with different guys.”



Crevier has been the most successful seventh rounder so far from that 2020 draft with 134 games played, with Ilya Solovyov of the Pittsburgh Penguins behind him at 45 games and a guy who featured in the Rochester local news shoveling his sidewalk (Devon Levi) in third with 39 games played.
